c.b: 1st pendant is not hard to find. Should have no problems. 2nd Pendant took me a week, and I swore I would help future druids with this awful quest with simple and accurate directions. Once you get to Westfall, through however means, make your way to Sentinel Hill. If this is your first trip, and you have to walk, then set an hour of your life aside and pack a lunch. It's a long trip. I totally recommend you stop in Ironforge, Stormwind and Sentinel Hill to get new flight paths from the Gryphon Masters so that you NEVER have to walk that trip again. Side Note - Once in West Falls, and on your way to Sentinel Hill, you may notice Moonbrook - Don't go in! This town is nasty. Full of aggressive humanoids. Just stick to the paths as much as possible. You don't want to die in this area. This is not a friendly area and you may always be resurrecting into trouble. Once in Sentinel Hill (which is friendly, by the way), make your way, however you want, to the ocean. Beware the trip, because there are beasts everywhere you go. So, wherever you end up on the beach, just make sure on your mini map that you are lined up directly across from Sentinel Hill and the Quarry. Head out into the ocean. Again, watch for beasts. Swim straight out until you reach the end of the reef. If you go further, you will fatigue. Turn right, take a deep breath and swim down until you get a good view of the ocean floor. Continue swimming straight in this direction coming up for air, of course, until you see the anchor. (You will probably need to come up about 3 times for air before you can see the anchor.) It is embedded on the ocean floor, just on edge of the reef. Long and black, only half of it is visible. Come up for air, then go down to anchor, there is a small ridge behind it on the deep side of the reef. You will have to swim very, very deep to get to this reef, but it will be fine. There is a bubbly fissure on the ridge that you can right click on to breathe in it's air. Open the chest next to the bubbly fissure and collect your pendant. Teleport back and complete remaining tasks for quest. Good luck, and you are gonna love your aquatic form. Much easier to swim as a sea lion!

I've done this twice now and have found a pretty simple way to do it. Bring plenty of food and drink, 10 each should do. On the lower level lock/VW pairs, open with a corruption on the lock and have your imp start attacking about a half second after you start casting. Followup up with an immolate, then 1-2 shadowbolts. You'll be tanking the VW during this, and even in grays/whites you should be around half health or so when the lock drops. Now have your imp attack the VW and pull it off of you, then drop a CoA, corruption, immolate on the VW and followup with a shadowbolt. You can melee it down from there provided you get no resists, and you and your imp should both survive the fight, albeit low on health. Eat/drink and move on. If you don't mind dying (and it's much faster to), then when you get to the 14s get close, but not too close. Have the imp attack the lock, and as soon as the firebolt lands, run over and loot the chest. This takes a little bit of timing, because you need to start running over to the chest as soon as the lock starts casting and the VW aggros on your imp. This is why you don't want to get as close as possible, because the imp is going to die before the chest is open and you need enough distance from the VW to finish looting. It helps if you autoloot. Then start running out along the southernmost path and hug the wall, you should be able to rez from outside the cave if you do so. You could probably fear the VW as soon as the lock aggros on your imp and buy yourself more time, but I haven't tried that.

c.b: This isnt my work, but its a great post from elsewhere on the net. This map will help (Quest chain link 2 and 3 are in Durotar) Call of Fire 1.0 To find Kranal Fiss, start off by heading West out of Razor Hill (where you most likely picked up the quest). On your way out the gate, go ahead and pick-up the Consription of the Horde(?) quest which sends you into the Barrens anyhow. Follow the road directly west until you cross over the Southfury by way of the bridge and hand-in the recommendation letter quick. Continue west up the hill and along the road. Just as you reach the top of the hil you will notice two buildings off to your right set against the mountains. Karnal Fiss is here. Your trial of fire awaits... Call of Fire 1.1 ** The path up to this next quest giver is the thinest I have seen in the game yet. Walk carefully. As Fiss has just politely explained, you are now ready to start playing with fire! Though, unlike before, this right of passage actually involves a bit of footwork and elbow grease to claim. First you will need to carry the Torch of the Dormant Flame to one Telf Joolam, a troll shaman high on the peak of a mountain in southern DUROTAR (NOT the Barrens!). From Fiss' place, hit the road once more and head east back down the hill and over the Southfury bridge. Now stop. Turn to your right. You should be facing south now. Follow the EASTERN bank of the Southfury until you come to a rather large mountain that, lo-and-behold, encompasses most of The Den and the Valley of Trials. Nifty. What you're looking for is a path up the mountain marked by a small blue stone that resembles a miniature obelisk (36,57). Take the path 'til it splits and veer to your right. Watch your footing here as the trail winds you around the mountain a bit and becomes rather narrow at more than a few points. After some mild hiking you will have reached the summit, and your goal: Telf Joolam. Congrats! You're one step closer to starring in a re-make of Firestarter. Call of Fire 1.2 Nothing in life is free - at least, nothing good. Like many before him, good ol' Joolam is both untrusting and lazy. You'll need to track down a couple reagents for him to properly prepare your next sapta. Fear not though, the worst part of this little collection is the running back and forth. Fire Tar Drops off pretty much any razormane caster; Mystics and Geomancers are closest, in the Barrens @ Thorn Hill 73,18 (just slightly north east of x-roads). Reagent Pouch Head out the back gate of Razor Hill located at 54,40 (right next to the Warlock & Demon trainers). head up the hill going directly north and continue on until you see a cave. This is your destination, Dustwind (53.29 Durotar)- NOT Skull Rock - Cave. Inside kill Neophytes until the pouch drops. Got mine on kill number eleven. Pretty quick and easy. Now to hoof it all the way back to Joolam. Call of Fire 1.3 Go past Joolam and stand before the giant obelisk. Drink your Fire Sapta. Continue up to the top of the mountain. Don't worry about the many smaller fire elementals roaming the outer edge of the mountain top. They won't get involved. The Minor Manifestation of Fire mob you need to defeat is level 12 and non-hostile. Take your time readying up and then go to it. At level 11 I beat him down in all of 6 seconds. Way easy. Hand in the quest at the brazier, transforming your Torch of the Dormant Flame into a Torch of the Eternal Flame. time to bring it back to Fiss and collect us some fire power, baby. Call of Fire 1.4 Go see Fiss. Collect your Fire Totem, along with a new spell - Searing Totem - and your XP. Throw back some brew, drop the new totem and /dance your butt off. >:D

c.b: I did this solo at level 20 with green gear and 11 points into Holy. I failed it the first time but managed to do it on my second try. I have a few tips: First, use Retribution Aura. The Defias Raiders don't have a ton of HP, and it will weaken the rest down while you concentrate on one. The first time I tried and failed was with Devotion. Second, use Consecrate to grab initial aggro on the wave, and use it once or twice more during each fight. Same idea as Ret aura; it will beat all the Raiders down so by the time you get to the last one they will die in 1 or 2 hits. Third, fight close to Daphne. If you fight close enough to her she will run up and melee with you. Between Ret aura and Consecrate she won't pull aggro, but you could use Righteous Fury just to be safe =) Finally, bring some Melon Juice. You do get time to drink between waves but your time is limited. PS - Can't hurt to make sure LoH is up! Good luck to all =)

c.b: For those new to this chain, make sure you talk to Duthorian Rall in the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind before going to find her. To find her, go to the Deadmines exit and follow the dirt path around back (not inside the cave, around the mountain.) She will be in the orchard, and will walk to the house before the waves start coming. The mobs are lvl 16-18 defias who were pretty easy to defeat, even for this undergeared just-turned-20 palladin. Tips: * Use Consecration early and often. It just destroys them, and you get time to recharge your mana after each fight. * Use Retribution aura, as they hit fast but weak. * Kill with Daphne - Click on her, then press 'f' to get her target. The mobs will go down much faster if you two are working together. * Use a board & sword (or mace, as the case may be.) That extra defense and mitigation will come in very handy with all of their small strikes. I only had to shield once, and I probably could have even healed through that. This should be pretty easy for most people.

Just soloed the entire quest at level 22. It CAN be done. The Ore Shipment is cake since Blizz nerfed the ogres in Loch Modan. The Kor Gem is just a lot of running to get to BFD. You have to go underwater and into the cave, but you don't need to enter the actual instance. The tricky part starts with the smithing hammer. The pulls in SFK are all 2 at a time, if done right, and very easily managed (I didn't need to exit the portal, but I suppose you could do that if you're not burning pots/scrolls/elixirs). As said above, the one death in the jail cell area is unavoidable - that boss simply cannot be taken down alone at that level. All I did was jump down, bubble, open the cell and talk to the NPC, and then died. As long as you don't release until the dude gets the door open, you can run back and finish up with minimal effort. First of all, this quest is for level ten and above only. It follows the Vejrek quest- right after that’s finished, go to the Great Forge in Ironforge. Right in the middle of the forge is the trusty yellow question mark- and that’s how Ironband’s compound quest gets started. After receiving the quest, prepare for a long walk and then a lot of little battles. If able, equip a gun or bow with lots of ammo. Now, leave Irongforge. Follow the path down until you’re back in regular Dun Morogh. When the path reaches the bottom of the hill, take a left onto the path. Then take your first available right. Then STAY ON THE PATH for a very long walk. You’ll get to a road sign that points to Gol’ Bolar Quarry. This is when you stray off the path- go towards Gol’Bolar Quarry but stay on the outskirts of it. If you go around it, towards the mountains, you’ll reach Iraonban’ds Compound, directly in between Helm’s Bed Lake and Gol-Bolar Quarry. Be careful on your approach- there are a ton Rockjaw Ambushers. Go slow and pick them off one by one. Lucky for you, most of the Ambushers can be looted for coins (I got decently rich off this quest, for a bit anyway). Once past them, you’ll get to the Dark Iron Spys. Be careful because those will gang up on you if they get the chance- if you’re fighting two at once, try using Thunder Clap, which will deal damage to both enemies at the same time. Once in the house, there are two Dark Iron Spys. After finishing them off, go down the stairs to the basement, where you’ll fight the big guy. He goes down pretty easy. In the corner of the basement there should be a shimmering box- open it up for your reward. Once the umbral ore is obtained, high tail it back to the Great Forge. There, you’ll receive the weapon of your choice. Good job!

c.b: It appears that the 3 named mobs at the house in Brackwell Pampkin Patch always spawn together, and would not respawn until all three is dead. So if you go to the house and can't find Surena Caledon, kill the rest first -- then Surena will respawn (along with others). This most likely isn't a bug ... devs presumably made it this way so that even unexperienced players can clear the house solo by using "hit-and-run" tactics (this is a level 10 quest after all ... chain fearing **shouldn't** be the only solution to it). So if you're pretty good and can clear all three at once, praise unto thee, otherwise, here's a much simpler version of clearing the place at level 10: 1. Clear the area around the house. 2. Start casting your non-instant DoT (Immolate or Corruption) on Surena or Erlan. 3. While casting your first DoT, command your Imp to attack the same mob (Ctrl+1 or mouse-click the action bar). 4. Apply the rest of DoTs and run. 5. When you come back, there'll be only two of them. Now it should be very easy ... fear & conquer! What probably happens if you follow this, would be: Morgan putting a Gauge on you and turning to your Imp. So don't panic, concentrate on getting the DoTs on the first mob and run. I believe that's the way devs probably had in mind when they designed the encounter -- you can probably follow it even if this Lock is your very first toon.

c.b: You can accept the beginning of this questline at level 20,but it strongly suggests to be done at level 30. Reason being is you'll travel to the corners of the world where most of the mobs needed for this quest are near level 30. This quest can be completed in any manner you desire. Needless to say there is no order to aqcuire any of these items. However I'll list the format I used along with some Tips that I'd reccomend considering. : Before you embark on your Journey,switch your hearth to Stormwind temporarily. It'll make this quest much more easier Step 1.) Begin by flying to Thelsamar,assuming you have the Flight Path already. You will then want to travel down to Thelgen Rock which is relatively close near the network of tunnels leading down to The Wetlands. Once you see cluttering spiders engage in combat and begin looting Fangs. : Activate Retaliation and pull about 2-3 spiders at a time. In theory you should gather more fangs this way :) Step 2.) Immediately after your done hearth back to Stormwind and go to the Harbor. Find the wharf that is decorated in Night Elf architecture and wait for the boat. This boat leads to Auberdine now,evidently taking this will bring you closer to Stonetalon Mountains. Once you've arrived in Auberdine fly to Astranaar,once again assuming you have this Flight Path already. If not a quick stroll to this town won't take long. : On your way to Astranaar,stop by Grove of the Ancients and do the quest The Sleeper Has Awakened from Kerlonian Evershade. This is fast exp and it follows the road to Astranaar. Step 3.) Now pass by Astranaar and go southeast until you reach a tunnel called Talondeep Path. It's a very obvious landmark in the side of the mountain. Picture. You'll exit out of the path into Windshear Crag,Stonetalon Mountains. Avoid the mobs and run to the major road. Follow it until theres several forks at Mirkfallon Lake. Go to the road guarded by Rogue Flame Spirits. Keep going until you reach The Charred Vale. Your objective now is to kill Chimaeras in this area and take their Horns. : The Chimaera Matriarch wanders the southern Hemisphere of the Vale or if you look on your map she dwells underneath the words "The Charred Vale". Watch out for Harpies too! The Final Step You now have every item besides the Vial of Phlogiston. This is the most difficult portion of the quest as it takes place in an Instance in Horde Territory. It really doesn't get any more agonizing than that. If you can,find a group for Roogug or for a full run. You could also whisp a friend to give you a quick run through. Ultimately this is pretty straight forward. Kill the Boss,loot the vial then undoubtedly your Hearth to Stormwind should be ready. If it isnt and you have a gathering profession you could run around increasing your skill more. : If by coincidence,you have some quests for RFK it'd be best to do a full run of the Instance. A full run could also occupy time for your Hearth to reactivate. Above all watch out for Horde on a PvP server! If you get caught in this situation take advantage of your Racial Abilities ;) Enjoy your new Fire Hardened Hauberk!

I found this quest both difficult and the posts fragmented which made it hard to understand so I thought I'd provide a step-by-step walkthrough. I completed this at Lvl 30 but had a lvl 30 Priest with me most of the time and called in some Guildies in the 50s to help with the Elementals. I don't think this quest is possible at lvl 30 without some level 40+ players to help. Suggestion: There's LOTS of travel for this quest. You might want to run through to Refugee Point in Arathi Highlands and over to Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills to get the flight paths to save some time getting to Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands (assuming you need to take the boat to Booty Bay in StrangleThorn Vale). You need to complete three separate tasks BEFORE you return to Bath'rah and fight a Level 40 Wind Elemental to earn the Whirling Axe (which appears to be the best choice). The first is to find 8 Liferoot, this is easy to purchase from the Auction House in any major city. The second is to get 30 BloodTusks from Trolls (lvls 34-36) in the Northern portion of Stranglethorn Vale (STV) Coords: 25,10. This is a long trip and there are often tons of horde in the same area. The Trolls can be pulled but often you're figthing 2-3 at a time. The final step is to get 8 Thundering, Burning and Cresting charms from elementals (lvls 38+) in the Arathi Highlands (note: I bought a number of Cresting Charms in the Auction House). These things are tough and with two level 30 characters (Warrior and Priest) we weren't able to kill them, we needed some level 50s to help. Thundering Charm (8) = Thundering Exile | Arathi Highlands | 50,53 Burning Charm (8) = Burning Exile | Arathi Highlands | 26,26 Cresting Charm (8) = Cresting Exile | Arathi Highlands | 67,30 Bring all of the things you collected back to the Cauldron near Bath'rah where you should see a Question Mark, the charms will create the Essence of the Exile. Hand everything in to Bath'rah and follow him to fight the Lvl 40 Wind Elemental. I earned two levels in the process of completing this quest and the Axe doubled the amount of damage I was delivering (so I thought it was worth it).

If you fight him in berserker stance, or at least switch to berserker stance when he knocks back, you will be able to intercept back onto him while in mid-air, taking no fall damage. c.b: As already mentioned, Cyclonian is easily soloable by drinking a Nature Protection Potion. There are a few other points that may facilitate the fight: - Drink your first Nature Protection Potion right after speaking with Bath'rah the Windwatcher. When Cyclonian is at about 50% health your potion-cooldown will be ready again. Use a second pot if necessary. - Activate the cast bar in your interface-options. Now you can see when Cyclonian starts to cast Gust of Wind as well as Whirlwind and avoid the effect. You can avoid the effect of both, Gust of Wind and Whirlwind, by staying away from Cyclonian while he casts. - Always fight Cyclonian with your back to the walls of the old ruins surrounding the spot Bath'rah the Windwatcher summons Cyclonian. Cyclonian will use Knock Away. By fighting with your back to the walls you will avoid the fall damage every time he uses it. - Use your cooldowns. There's no reason to not use Berserker Rage if you fight in Berserker stance, Retaliation if you fight in Battle Stance or Shield Wall if you fight in Defensive Stance. As far as I tested, Cyclonian's normal attacks do nature damage but can be counterattacked. - Cyclonian is immune to Charge's Charge Stun. I didn't test if he's also immune to Shield Bash, Pummel and Concussion Blow. I fought Cyclonian as a level 38 Protection Warrior with 2201 health points and no buffs by other classes. I wielded Sword of Serenity and Heart of Agamaggan.

Once you get the quest to obtain the Heartswood, use your Hearthstone and go back to Astranaar...go to the ruins of Ordil'Aran and approach from the south. c.b: I'd like to add the following information: the pre-crit per-hit damages* of each weapon, prior to any talents: Whirlwind Axe: 102-154 damage, average 128 Whirlwind Warhammer: 97-146 damage, average 121.5 Whirlwind Sword: 82-124 damage, average 103 Pure Damage Benefits of WWA over WWWH: average 6.5 more damage per Whirlwind, Mortal Strike, or Slam average 3.75 more damage per Overpower 1.3 + AP/350 damage per tick with Rend 3.12 damage per tick with Deep Wounds Pure Damage Benefits of WWA over WWS: average 25 more damage per Whirlwind, Mortal Strike, or Slam average 12.5 more damage per Overpower 5 + AP/140 damage per tick with Rend 12 damage per tick with Deep Wounds Pure Damage benefits of WWWH over WWS: average 18.5 more damage per Whirlwind, Mortal Strike, or Slam average 9.25 more damage per Overpower 6.17 + AP/233.3 damage per tick with Rend 8.88 damage per tick with Deep Wounds These are the only warrior attacks which benefit from higher average weapon damage at this level, and white damage should, over time, be the same all Whirlwind Weapons. Myself, I see the racial expertise benefits as more useful than the slight pure damage lead that the WWA has over the WWWH for humans and dwarves, but at least now the exact benefits are spelled out. * I purposely refrain from saying "top end damage" because people are incorrect in using it. What matters is the average weapon damage, which is just the average of top and bottom damage. This is more accurate, since instant cast attacks don't always use the top damage, they randomly determine the damage between the min and the max.

c.b: TATTERED MANUSCRIPT COORDINATES: Varies - begins at 46, 68ish, Hillsbrad MOLDY TOME COORDINATES: 44, 37 --Tattered Manuscript-- You may want to start with this one since its a little closer to where you pick the quest up. The manuscript is being held smack dab in the middle of a murloc camp. The manuscript looks like a little nondescript book just laying in the sand among the other debris of the camp. The manuscript spawns at a random camp so no definite coordinates can be given but the camps are located southwest of the human town of Southshore and start at 46, 68. There are quite a few murlocs so you might want to get some friends to help you slaughter the murlocs and grab the manuscript but this quest is soloable. One tactic that Ive had luck with is running out to the hilly area behind each murloc camp and using the Eye of Kilrogg to scout out the camp. Once Ive located the manuscript, Ill clear the area of any murlocs leading up to the camp, send in the Voidwalker to gather aggro, grab the manuscript then run away, sacrificing the VW if neccesary. This technique can also be used on the ocean side of the camps if you prefer however your escape will be hindered by murlocs and the fact that you will be swimming rather than running. --Moldy Tome-- The Moldy Tome is located within the cave Splinterhoof Hold located in Thousand Needles coordinates 44, 37. After entering the cave, branch right as soon as you're able. Follow this path past the waterfall until you see a small chest labeled "Damaged Chest". This contains the tome which you seek. The centaurs in the cave are slightly stronger than the ones outside. Centaurs flee when their health is low so keep Curse of Recklessness handy; you don't want a centaur running off and aggroing the whole cave. Also, be wary of the Lightning Cloud that the Stormers cast.

c.b: Smoky Iron Ingots: - These drop off of the Windshear Kobolds in the Stonetalon Mountains. The mine is on the eastern part of the map, to the south east of Venture Company HQ. The highest rate of drops came from the diggers, but they all dropped them quickly. The Kobolds are in the 22-24 range, and once you get in the mine, they will sometimes group up into 2-4 total. At level 30, they were easy, but if you are lower, bring a friend. It took me about 10 minutes to get all the ingots. Flogiston: - This drops off of Roogug in Razorfen Krawl. Razorfen Krawl is located at the very southern end of the Barrens near the Great Lift. The Great DGDough's location description is perfect, and you shouldn't have any trouble finding him if you go that route. He is a 28 elite and will have a Shaman and Warrior with him. Also has a pet, all elite. To get to him, you have to fight through several 25-27 elites also. If you are high enough, you may be able to pick your way through to him, but it would be tough. I tried it with a 32 Warrior because I have had trouble getting a group to go to that part of the dungeon, and got to Roogug and couldn't kill him because all the mobs pull at the same time. As a side note, lots of mining veins in there and I also found some Fadeleaf and tons of Briarthorn. This is probably the hardest part of the quest because you need a group willing to kill this guy unless you level enough to solo it, and then the armor would not be worth it. Powdered Azurite: - This drops off of Hillsbrad Miners in the southwestern portion of Hillsbrad. The miners are all 25-28 in level and there are some wandering Foremen in the area. At 32, it was easy to solo. Only had one close call with a boss foreman (30: non-elite) who summoned a pet and another foreman to help. It took about 30 minutes to go through the mine and collect the 10 pieces of Azurite. Iron Bars - Easy. Either mine it or buy it from the AH. That is it, hopefully it helps anyone who wants to do the quest. The other bonus to the quest is you get over 6000 xp for completing it (at level 34) and the other three armor quests unlock, which are significantly easier than this. -Allakhazam.com

c.b: This comment may seem redundant, but I just wanted to clear up and verify the information from previous comments. I just followed these steps today (Aug 26, 2007). When I read all of the comments here, I got a little confused. Hopefully this will help. If not, feel free to rate it down. Basically, as soon as you take the quest, grab one of the lunchbox-looking things (Chest of Containment Coffers) and one of the scrolls (Cantation of Manifestation) from the table next to Jennea Cannon. Head to the Blue Recluse (approximately at 38,84). If you're entering the Mage Quarter from the Trade District and you take the southern path inside the quarter after the tunnel, it should be the first building on your left. But, you'll probably be heading there from the Mage's Tower, so as soon as you get outside, jump off the right side and you should see the building. Then, follow the advice of adders666 (six posts above this one). I followed his instructions and it worked perfectly. To reiterate, summon the first one in the basement, then go up the stairs and summon from within the fireplace, then go into the main room and go under one of the staircases to summon. For each summon, once you've stunned the creature, use the Chest of Containment Coffers. This will throw a coffer onto the ground and the creature will become trapped in it. Pick up the coffer once it's filled. Do this for each creature. Once you have three of them, head back to Jennea.
This reminds me so much of Ghostbusters. After you stun them you throw down the trap to dispose of them. A job well done!!

rep.b: As of Patch 2.3, they made getting to Tabatha a lot easier by making a path toward her house. Now that these wands have the same stats (+3 Int, +7 spellpower) you'd likely be best off taking the Nether Force Wand, as it has the highest dps (marginally, but it's there) if/when you go oom.

c.b: Just completed this today as a moderately geared 36 frost mage. With him being six levels higher than me it was very difficult to hit him even with Elemental Precision (Resist chance -3%) The boss will splinter off and create adds every 20% damage he takes, when he does this his melee damage drops dramatically though. Each splinter seems to drop his damage by about 20% or so down to around 10-40 or so once fully debuffed. The first splinter was the most difficult to pull off as he starts off the fight hitting like a freight train hitting a stalled bus full of orphans, nuns and puppies (about 300-400 on cloth... ouch.) Like everyone else has said, start off the fight at max range, put up the mana shield and frost / fire ward then nuke him as hard as possible before he can get to you. (May need to run out if first fire/ice-bolt is resisted or reflected.) Once he's down to 80% he'll shard and spawn the add... I had to run out at this point as it took everything I had to just drop him 20% the first time. Then with each set of adds I would blizzard at max range then frost nova, cone of cold, arcane explosion them down and run for the exit again. This got much easier as the splinter debuffs stacked and even reduced the numbers of attempts taken to splinter him again. Once he was fully debuffed I got to start the long part of wanding him to death. This was remakably easy to do, even at 36, by just keeping mana shield up and wanding him down. He will still spawn his adds every 20%, but they are easy to deal with by just frost novaing, then CoC & Arcane Explosion til dead. I had Gift of the Naaru to heal myself, and for a mage it's pretty much a full heal every 3 minutes, and evocated twice to keep my mana up. All in all this process took me about an hour. Probably woulda been smarter to get somebody to help me, but this way does work too.

c.b: How to solo: Stay on the steps (top of the steps is fine) and right click on the scroll. One ghost will spawn closer to you than the others. Do your frost nova so you ONLY get one in the trap. Then run, the other 3 will follow you a very short way, then they will disappear. As soon as they disappear, the 4th one (the one you trapped) will be after you. Kite it back to the store, and kill it there (easiest way is frost nova again inside the area, then blast it). Capture it in the containment coffer (by right clicking on the box in your stash), it will suck the spirit into the coffer, and you right click once more on the coffer on the floor. Repeat twice more. Pretty easy once you get the hang of it. Just make sure you only trap one.

c.b: This is entirely doable solo at 20 if you're mildly twinked and remember to use the weaknesses of each mob. Being 22 would help of course seeing as you have access to skills like distract and vanish. Some notes of my own to add to the above post: - Part 1, Pickpocketing Make sure to approach Silixiz from behind and use pickpocket as far away as possible (5 yd range), otherwise he's sure to detect you. Kill him afterwards, both as a courtesy to the next rogue coming to do the quest and in order to avoid him aggro'ing on you in case you have to run away during the rest of the quest. - Part 2, Mutated Drones This seems to be the hardest part. Be very careful and only approach one of them when they turn their backs to you and spam ambush till it connects (their stealth detection is insanely high). Then run till you drop aggro and do the same with the other one. - Part 3, Patrolers These mobs are weak to rupture, but they're very easy to kill even without it. Probably the easiest part, just good ol' hack n slash works on these guys. - Part 4, Lookouts Nothing else to say about them really... just get that 1 CP as fast as possible and immediately Eviscerate. Very easy to kill that way. - Part 5, Gallywix Make sure to have Evasion and healing potions ready and not cooling down before engaging. Open with Ambush to drop him to 50% health, then immediately pop Evasion (he hits very hard, you don't want to waste a moment without it up) and just hack away. Pop a healing potion if necessary. If you're close to dying, make sure he's facing away from the stairway entrance. Didn't try this myself, but supposedly if you die with him facing the stairs, he'll stay in that position when he resets making it nearly impossible to ambush him without being detected. Another note: You do ABSOLUTELY want to use Ambush in the parts that recommend it and you need a dagger in your main hand for that. If you've been using two swords up to this point, get a dagger for this quest. Even if it's a level 1 grey one, doesn't matter, you can just switch to your usual weapon right after you Ambush. Also, be sure to get your dagger skill up to a decent level, you don't want your Ambush to miss.

I’ll simply summarize quickly. 1- (outside on the left) You need to pickpocket the key from Silixiz. If he doesn't have anything to pickpocket, kill him and wait for him to respawn. He only gives one key per respawn. To be nice to the next guy, I would kill him after you have the key. 2- (First floor): Mutated Drones. Key Ability: Ambush kills them in one shot. You can ambush one, sprint away. Then come back and ambush the other. 3- (Second floor) Patrollers. Key Ability: Rupture takes off extra damage. 4- (Outside - third floor): Lookouts. Key Ability: Eviscerate turns them into weak oozes. A one pointer will transform them into green slimes that are easy to kill. 5- (Top floor) Gallywix. Key Ability: Ambush. It does 50% of his health in damage. Ambush him to lower his life to 50%, then the rest of the fight is as you would expect. You might have to gouge/bandage and pop evasion to finish him, but he is killable at 20. If you wait till 22, you can Ambush then vanish and Ambush again. After he's dead, take his head and lockpick the chest (need skill ~85 I think) and you're done. IF GROUPED: When you group w/ someone else who has this quest, you have to each pickpocket the key off Silixiz and each loot the dead body of Gallywix for the head. This means that you have to: a) pickpocket the key b) kill Silixiz and wait for the respawn c) pickpocket the key again for the 2nd player (repeat for next guy) e) after killing Gallywix only have 1 of you loot the body and chest (you'll need to wait for respawn and kill him again and whoever loots will get the poison debuff) DONT LOOT THE CHEST UNTIL YOU HAVE THE HEAD. You will get a 7 day debuff that lowers agility and makes it easier to detect you in stealth. This quest is a good opportunity for warlocks to have a lot of fun with Enslave Demon. The large variety of satyrs in the area results in many different sets of abilities for you to control. Your slave won't be able to hold aggro, but the satyrs are spaced out enough so your target will rarely aggro more if you Fear it, and if you do aggro more, that's what Banish is for. Hatefury Betrayers and Felsworn don't do anything, so don't bother with them, and Rogues can stealth, which is kind of useless. Hellcallers have Immolate and Rain of Fire. Tricksters have a poison DoT. Shadowstalkers have Gouge and Backstab. Remember that even though these abilities are on auto-cast, the slaves will use them whenever their AI tells them to, so you may need to manually click on them in order to hurry things along. Also note that since they're NPCs, their abilities can't be interrupted through damage.

This quest is do-able at the time when the quest is received, I received it around level 29, but started it at level 31. The Hatefury Satyr can be found in the north east corner of Desolace, and the Lesser Infernal (http://www.wowhead.com/?npc=4676) can be found by following the path south, the one that doesn't lead to the graveyard, to Feralas. Also found in that location will be Mana Eaters (needed for the Fragments of the Orb of Orahill quest (http://www.wowhead.com/?quest=1799) also a Warlock Quest), a few Succubi, as well as a few humanoids. The Lesser Infernal is around level 35-36, so it isn't an easy fight as it is a very tight area.

c.b: Burning Exiles can be killed at level 31 if you stock up on Cresting Charms (http://www.wowhead.com/?item=4481), either through the AH or through a higher-level alt farming Cresting Exiles. Gather enough charms, "tag" the mob by doing some damage with a spell (it has to be *your* damage, not your pet's!), then simply right-click the charm to kill the exile immediately. As long as you tagged it, you can loot it. Getting the initial "tag" is the hard part at level 31 as the resist rate is very high. I found using my VW to tank as long as possible - then saccing him if needed - was a good way to buy me the time needed to get a few points of spell damage on the Exiles' health bars.

c.b: This quest, as the quick facts box indicates, is an available prequest to the standard priest quest of "fortify and renew x friendly faction member that is out in the forest." This also, like other versions, takes the player from their starting area to the next general leveling zone. In each case (all races with priests have a variation of this quest), the end of the chain results in a cloth, uncommon-quality robe with +1 spirit. When a new player completes all of the quests in a starting zone, a quest to proceed to the next town is offered. Because of this, it's recommended that you complete all of the starting-area quests before accepting this one, as it may potentially save you a trip. It is likely you will also find a quest along the way to the next town to deliver some form of goods to the next town's innkeeper, so you can really complete 3 quests in one short trip.
This is a priest only quest (which people may not notice if they just look at the fact box (like me))

Take note that if you're one of the people who likes to make a character and start in a different starting area, (for example, making a human priest and starting at the NE starting place) this quest will not be offered to you, even if you are a priest. c.b: 0.) Ask the trainer in Orgrimmar for the letter - right click and start the quest 1.) Must be level 24 - with Detect Traps 2.) Head to the Zepplin out side of Orgrimmar 3.) Take the Zellplin to UC (Undertcity) 4.) Take the Bat to Tarren Mill. If you don'thave the FP (Flight Path) then head to Silverpine Forest - head south and enter Hillsbrad Foothills. Follow the road and use your mini map. Pass the Alliance town (Southshore). Once your close enough to TM it will have a arrow pointing to the location of it - follow the arrow untill you reach TM. Get the FP. 5.) Start from the Bat Handler and head east to the river. Once at the river you'll see land on the other side. 6.) Cross the river and get to the other side. 7.) Once on the other side you should see a HUGE tree with a mountain behind it and two paths to go around it (Take whichever path you wish for it is not important). Though I perfer the right path around the mountain. 8.) Once your behind the mountain look up for there you'll see a zig-zag pathway up the mountain. 9.) Head up the mountain and follow the dirt road. 10.) Once your at the top you'll see level 50 Neutral Guards and behind them you see the tunnel! 11.) No need to stealth past the Guards for they wont attack you at all. 12.) Turn on 'Detect Traps' 13.) Enter the tunnel. 14.) Upon entering the tunnel you should see the chest! Hovering above the chest you should see a blue rectangle. 15.) Head towards the chest, but DO NOT OPEN IT! Once your close enough the quest update should have activated. 16.) Keep going through the tunnel and you end at the Manor. 17.) Head to the building and talk with Fahrad - BOOM quest completed!! Step-by-step instructions for an ALLIANCE warlock. - Note1: Alliance will refer mainly to flight paths I take. - Note2: If you SAVE this quest chain for level 80, you will get max level gold bonus awards. - Note3: You'll want to have completed the quest chain to get the key for Scholomance. - Note4: You'll need the key to Dire Maul. - Note5: If you get to part 3, you can save yourself a bit of money if you have a warlock friend who still has the items you need. ----- PART 1 Save Hearth in Dalaran and have it free. From Dalaran... Take the portal to Stormwind, go to the Auction House and buy all needed supplies: 1 Arcanite Bar 3 Black Dragonscale 2 Elixir of Shadow Power 6 Large Brilliant Shard 25 Dark Iron Ore Also have at least 406g in your pocket. From SW, FLY to Morgan's Vigil in Burning Steppes and take the road far to the west to the quest NPCs. Get QUESTS Rage of Blood and Lord Banehollow. BUY potions from the goblin for 6g. HEARTH back to Dalaran and take the portal to Darnassus. From Rut'theran Village, FLY to Talonbranch Glade in Felwood. Run south to Jaedenar, drink potion and go all the way back into Shadow Hold, as far as you can go. Do the bidding of Lord Banehollow, BUY the stardust from his orc minion for 150g. Run out of Shadow Hold and south to Emerald Sanctuary. FLY to Winterspring. In Winterspring, go north east from Everlook to find the highest concentration of Owlbeasts. Kill for quest item. HEARTH back to Dalaran and take portal to Stormwind, FLY to Burning Steppes and turn in quests. PART 2 Talk to the NPCs until you have the next 4 QUESTS: Imp Delivery, Bell of Dethmoora, Wheel of the Black March, Doomsday Candle. Here is where those supplies you bought earlier come in. From there, go north to Thorium Point in Searing Gorge. FLY to Chillwind Camp, Western Plaguelands and head to Scholomance. Inside Scholo: go past that first room and through the door. Go down the stairs to the LEFT and straight to the next door into the Chamber of Summoning. Go to the back of that room and through the door. Turn LEFT again and go through that room toward The Great Ossuary and all the way back, down the stairs. Kill the miniboss Rattlegore for the KEY to the next area. Go back up through The Great Ossuary and turn RIGHT and head through that door. Go RIGHT again and use your key on the door you see there. Then you will be in a large room (The Viewing Room) with a bunch of neutral NPCs. Go to the BACK RIGHT of that room, down the stairs into the room you need for the quest. In this room is the boss Ras Frostwhisper. The Alchemy Lab you need is in the right corner of the room after you enter (or looking at the map, top left). Kill those mobs, and release your Imp in a Jar. He will do his thing and the quest is complete. HEARTH back to Dalaran and take portal to Stormwind, FLY to Burning Steppes and turn in the 4 quests. Get the next quest, Arcanite and turn it in. The goblin now has all of the items you crafted for sale. Get the final quest: Dreadsteed of Xoroth. BUY J'eevee's Jar (150g), A Black Lodestone (50g), and Xorothian Glyphs (50g) from the goblin. PART 3 - Dire Maul Before heading to Dire Maul, make sure you have plenty of soul shards. If you are level 80, you won't be able to get any inside the instance. From there, go north to Thorium Point and FLY to Menethil Harbor, Wetlands. Take the boat to Theramore Isle. From Theramore, FLY to Feathermoon Stronghold and run to Dire Maul. For those who don't know, here is how this section of Dire Maul works: Dire Maul East and North are connected through a Library (a "safe" zone with a merchant and some neutral NPCs). You can go through DM East OR North, but for the purposes of this quest it's more convenient to go through DM East. The main boss, and the area you need to get to, is covered by a huge, impenetrable dome. In order to get inside you need to shatter the 5 wards that are placed throughout DM East. These wards are obvious, huge blue crystals with some arcane elementals around them. You kill the elementals and the ward shatters. When you go inside you see the FIRST ward immediately. Kill the elementals and move on ahead. Ahead, you will see a large ramp going down to a large tree boss, but do not go that way yet. Instead, go to the right, through the doorway, up the ramp there. There are the SECOND and THIRD wards on this upper level. Destroy them, go back down to the tree boss (killing him is optional) and through the door there. Next is a long hallway that leads to the final chamber. On either side of this chamber are the FOURTH and FIFTH wards that you need to break. Destroy them and the barrier is down. Kill Immol'thar. If you are NOT a skinner, kill him off to the side, or else his body will be on the location you need to use for the Summoning. PART 4 - The Summoning When you are ready, use J'eevee's Jar. He will come out and set up the bell, the wheel, and the candle (the instruments of empowerment). Now the fun starts... You will see 2 glowing pink circles, one inside the other, with the 3 instruments in the center. After J'eevee has placed the instruments down, the Circle will begin it's empowerment cycle. During the empowerment, many demons spawn on the outer edges of Immol'thar's prison. Wait for them to come to the center. Do not leave the center of the circle. Occasionally, you may notice that one of the instruments (bell, candle, wheel) has fallen. You simply right click it, and you use the Black Lodestone to repair it. This requires a soul shard. It is a cast spell and can be interrupted if you are hit. If you have trouble seeing if you need to repair, just mouse over the instruments occasionally. If you see the cog-wheel, you need to repair it. During this whole event, you may notice small runes appearing in between the inner and outer circle. These are the runes of empowerment, and they appear all around the circle. When they are complete, the event is over. Keep repairing the instruments (I noticed the candle got broken most often), and killing the demons until it's over. There are some shiny graphics and the demons you are fighting are recalled back to Xoroth and disappear. The Circle is now empowered and you can use your Xorothian Glyphs to summon the dreadsteed. Kill the dreadsteed, and the quest is complete. BUT WAIT! There's one more thing to do! The dreadsteed's master, Hel'nurath appears. Finish him off, talk to the Dreadsteed Spirit to complete your quest, and enjoy your Feat of Strength.

c.b: I soloed this as a level 70 affliction / demonology warlock without too many trouble. Here's a little guide: Go to the back entrance of Dire Maul in Feralas. The location is shown on the map Burgermeal posted, and it's pretty hard to miss. Just look for a structure with the same design as Dire Maul and head through the tunnel. When you're there, either open the door with the Crescent Key or Life Tap / Hellfire and revive your spirit at the other side of the door. When inside the instance, you'll see you skipped the entire elemental area of Dire Maul East and are at the demons you need straight away. Your Voidwalker is the one you'll love in here. First, you see two plants which aren't linked. Just pull them, drain tank a bit and they'll die without too many problems. Time for the real work now. In the area you'll find a couple of patrols which you'll want to pull first. They're not much stronger than a regular level ~68 mob, so you'll hardly have trouble with them. If you've cleared some patrols, it's time for the packs. Stick your Voidwalker on one Satyr, banish the Betrayer and DoT + drain tank the other Satyr. When your mob is down, kill the mob the Voidwalker is tanking and then kill the Betrayer which should be unbanished by now. This tactic will allow you to clear most of the area you need and should provide you with sufficient Satyr Bloods to complete the quest. Judging by the comments in this thread, many people seem to think there's also packs of four demons. This, however, is not the case. If you see a group of four demons, you'll see a normal group (of three demons) and a patrol. Just wait a second for the patrol to leave and do the normal routine. It might take a while for the patrol to leave, so don't bother trying four mobs at once (although it's probably possible), just head for another group or a patrol that isn't near a group. The droprate wasn't that high for me, so I actually had to reset the instance once and kill one or two more packs. It took me around 1,5 hours to complete this quest. Because I was in the demon area of DM East anyway, I figured it would be nice to try some bosses there, just for laughs. The first boss you'll encounter is Lethtendris who has an imp minion beside her. Just send your Voidwalker in, kill the imp (couple of DoT's and 1 or 2 shadow bolts should do) and then just Health Funnel your Voidwalker. If you have Siphon Life, keep it up to gain some extra health. I haven't tried drain tanking so I have no idea if that's actually possible, I just did it the safe way and do very slow DPS (the Siphon Life and sometimes a bit of wanding). You could also put an (amplified) Curse of Doom up, to speed things up a little without pulling aggro too soon of your Voidwalker. Once Lethtendris is dead, you can go downstairs and use exactly the same tactic on Hydrospawn. Both dropped a green for me, so I didn't actually profit from it, but it was quite fun, I guess... Anyway, once you're done with this quest, and the Prison's Casing quest, head back to the questgiver in Blasted Land and do the final part. Good luck!

Completed the entire quest line solo at level 66. There's a Doomguard Commander near 34.0, 63.0 that stands surrounded by a wide circle of Felguard Elites, they stands far enough from each other that I aggroed none of them. Send in your most capable tank minion on the commander and wait a few seconds to build a bit of aggro. With a little luck, he will waste his warstomp on your minion, if he does, don't waste a second and start channeling the prison. He won't do enough damage to kill you and only his stomp can interrupt. If he casts his rain of fire, you're home free as it lasts long enough to guarantee he won't stomp you until you're done! Keep in mind that none of the Felguard Elites around him can be enslaved - they are all immune, and it's a long corpse run to learn that lesson.

c.b: At level 74+ this quest can be done pretty quickly, due to being able to hearth/port from Dalaran. For Horde: Start in Orgimmar. If you don't have the flight path in Felwood, fly to your closest flight point which is either Crossroads, Barrens or some little outpost in Ashenvale. Note: If you don't have the Splintertree Post flightpath in Ashenvale already, it might be worth while to pick up before you head into Felwood so that you can fly there when heading to Azharra to save you a minute or two. Ride to Felwood, pick up the flightpath if you didn't already have it, and go find Impsy. Get this quest. Go to Jaedenar and do the escort quest, Rescue from Jaedenar, quickest way to get the fel essence to drop here; stated multiple times already. Fly to Splintertree Post then ride to Azharra and get the Fel Essence there. Hearth back to Dalaran and port to city of choosing. Find the mage portal to Blasted lands, kill the Fel Guards here. (I had issues finding some here, there are some on the sides by the mountains.) Go through the Dark Portal, fly to Shatt and portal to Orgrimmar. Fly to Felwood, turn in the quest and you're done with this part. For Alliance: Start in Darnassus. If you don't have the flight path in Felwood, fly to your closest flight point which will hopefully be Astranaar. If its not, you got some running to do. Fly/Ride to Felwood, pick up the flightpath if you don't have it, and go find Impsy. Get this quest. Go to Jaedenar and do the escort quest, Rescue from Jaedenar, quickest way to get the fel essence to drop here; stated multiple times already. Ride to Azharra and get the Fel Essence there. Hearth back to Dalaran and port to city of choosing. Find the mage portal to Blasted lands, kill the Fel Guards here. (I had issues finding some here, there are some on the sides by the mountains.) Go through the Dark Portal, fly to Shatt and portal to Darnassus. Fly to Felwood, turn in the quest and you're done with this part. Its pretty simple, but I hope it helps someone save a minute or two.

c.b: You will constantly see peasants with half health walking along, but resist the urge to heal them unless you see those bars dropping. HOWEVER, on the two peasants who are surrounded by the purple glow at the beginning of each new wave.. renew them. They're gonna take damage the whole time and you'll end up having to flash heal them more than once. Just renew. c.b: This is a very useful guide for all 70 Warlocks. I followed it myself as an affliction Warlock and it went smoothly. From thottbot, written by Shahwigs SOLO: 70 Demo lock, regular BC drop/quest gear. 1) Have the key to scholo... 2) Bring at least 10 shards, I did it with 5. 3) Curse on Weakness is your BEST friend here. 4) Enter scholo, 4 dead skelly warriors on the entry bridge. Single pull right and left front statics with Curse of Weakness. Dont send pet or you get ALL 4. The 2 in the back you will get together so just CoW them, throw some dots, tap tank, and HEAL Felguard. It's really not hard at 70 it seems, or CoW is just really awesome. 5)Open the door and pull the roaming skell warrior you see. Go in room, go down to the right side corner and pull the roamers to here as they walk by. You can clear the close statics if you want. Go left across the room and through the other gate. I pulled the right statics next to the door, 3 mobs, but probably didnt have too as the other side didnt aggro when I went through door. 6) Go in and turn left and you will see a long hall with 3 roamers and static bad guys on each side. You can ignore the statics and actually kill the roamers in the middle of the room without aggroing them. Go to the end of the room and open the gate. 7) 4 roamers in this next room and 2 come close enough to the door to pull them outside the room 1 at a time. when this is done, go in and turn left.Straight across this room is where your going, but you have 2 roamers left, further into this room. stay in the middle of the hall and pull the first roamer to you and kill it all quite like in the middle of the hall. Careful not to aggro the statics on both sides.. The three static mobs in the center of the room can be completely avoided. By far the most difficult quest I have ever done. Some quick tips are: Be dueling a warlock that you trust immensely while fighting Solenor, if you can keep him wing clipped, have aspect of the cheetah up at all times, you don't have to kill beetles. The reasoning for the warlock is for Curse of Recklessness (no fearing from Solenor). Simone's pet doesn't need to be killed, but you need to loot her head before he kills you. For Klinfran, if you are specced for Scatter Shot, you can kite to different ends of the Burning Steppes then use Scatter Shot and go the other way. He is leashed to only Burning Steppes, so no Redridge/BRM.

Solenor - A nice little tip for Solenor is when he starts off, drop a explosive trap and have him run into that. Then wing clip him and bolt outta there. The trap should to AoE damage to everything around him, and if you have curse of Recklessness on you, you shouldnt need to worry about the fears, so for the time the explosive trap lasts, you should have no problem with the bugs either. Just unload into him for when you can, but be sure you have a few mana pots on you and a shadow protection pot on you to keep the damage off you. Once the bugs start poping, and your trap wears off, when he's wing cliped git up volley rank 1 when you have all the bugs in a group. this should finish off the little suckers with use of the least mana as possible. This guy was the biggest pain for me personally, but that really just depends on what you're good at. Artorius - The main problem you WILL run into here, is getting around corners, and mana. So, when you start a turn, any turn at all, be sure to hit him in the face with a concussive shot, but dont get too far ahead of him in the process. Also, keep rank 1 arcane shot out like Kaenos said, and hit him with that every now and then between serpent stings to stay on his aggro list. I only shot him with the sting once every 3-5 seconds, because if you spam him, it will only stack up to 5 times, and your just wasting mana. The main thing to remember here besides the wait time on serpent sting is that rank 9 serpent sting DOESN'T work. One of my guildmates found this out the hard way, and only did minimal damage to him. This may have been updated in 2.0.1, but to the best of my knowledge, stick to sting rank 8. Simone - Basically easy to kill, i got her pet down first, and the killed her, but as long as you have nature protection pots and some mana pots on you just in case, you should be able to kite her around, even without killing her pet if you want to. Having another hunter follow you around with aspect of nature on is really good, because that allows you to keep aspect of the hawk on, which can really add to your DPS. Klinfran - Best thing to use here is rank one for wing clip. It gets the job done without wasting mana. The strat here can really be based on your weapon speed. Since each weapon has a specific attack speed (2.4s or whatever) once you scorpid sting him, you run up and attack him for 10 seconds. Your weapon can help time this, because if you have a 2.0 second attack speed, just hit him 5 times, wing clip and start running away. Try not to use raptor strike, because this fight is gonna be the longest one, and you will need the mana. When the fight starts off, hit him with concussive shot, frost trap, whatever you got to slow him down, and once he enrages hit him with scorpid. Then, start the attack cycle of running up, hitting him so many times, wing clip, run away, wait for enrage, and hit him with scorpid sting again. From there rince and repeat for roughly 7-10 minutes. Keep some mana pots with you for this fight specifically, and be sure to have a tuber or two for some health incase you slip up and he nails you once or twice. when you get far enough away from him after wing clipping him, you can hit him with an auto shot or two to add to some damage, but never try to aimed shot him. Also, don't use counterattack if it comes up. Imp wingclip can be helpful, but keep in mind you need to wait 10 seconds after you wing clip him for the enrage to come back up, and if you counterattack him, hes only stuck in place for 4 seconds, so he will be charging at you for 6 seconds, until he enrages, which most likely means hes gonna enrage within your minimum range. The most useful thing to use if this does happen though is scatter shot, then get away from him and hit him with a scorpid sting. You might get hit once or twice, but you should be able to survive 2-3 hits, and then just pick up where you left off and learn from your mistakes.

Completed this quest today as a lvl 61 protection pala, with help from a lvl 70 fury warrior. The final stage was relatively simple, as long as you run for a corner after placing the Scryer. From here you won't pull the entire room of ghosts at once, and can instead fight smaller groups of them using the correct judgement every time it's available. Also, be aware that simply attacking the ghosts with the correct seal applied appears to have a small chance to proc the AoE effect as well so don't leave everything to the people helping you. The effect cannot be refreshed though, so wait until it wears off before judging your seal if you get a proc from normal hits. Each wave of ghosts is followed by an Aspect, which is a larger and significantly tougher single ghost with similar vulnerabilities and attacks to its counterparts. The death of the Aspect of Shadow triggers Darkreaver to spawn, and both the Aspect and Darkreaver himself wil aggro on spawning no matter where you try to hide in the room. Because of this, your rest stop before Darkreaver should be taken before you pull the last of the regular Shadowed ghosts as once you spawn the Aspect you're in combat until Darkreaver is dead. Be ready to bubble if Darkreaver uses his mind control ability successsfuly, you don't want to get killed by accidental (or, of course, purposeful - some people love to take those kind of opportunities ;)) whirlwinds, cleaves and so on or get beaten down by a controlled part member. My level 70 counterpart resisted it once, and I bubbled out when he used it on me. When you start the fight, put the scryer as far as you can in the NW corner, and stand in the SE corner. For the first 2 waves, you can single-pull the spirits. Last two waves are groups of 3+. It's not a hard fight as long as your pally (or pallies) use the proper judgement on the mobs, I've done it with only the pally with the quest before with minimal problem. The order is Wisdom, Justice, Righteousness, Light. The spirits will have names that hint at what to use (Banality, Malice, Corruption, Shadow) At the end of each wave, an Aspect of (wave name) appears, basically supposed to be a miniboss for that wave, but they're easy. Once the boss comes up, he goes down quick and the pally has his mount!

rep.b: You need highest ranks in following Seals: * Seal of Wisdom (rank 3) -> Banality * Seal of Justice (rank 1) -> Malicious * Seal of Righteousness (rank 8) -> Corrupted * Seal of Light (rank 4) -> Shadowed or else your judgement does nothing. I wiped at the 3rd part because my seal wasnt rank 8.

Agreed. Standing at the SE corner alows you to drink/eat between waves. But beware of the last wave - once you pulled them, you'll have no breaks until the end of the quest. I was at 15% mana and health when finished shadow wave and it was hard to fight with last boss in such condition. Hard but not impossible. Did it solo with 68 proto pala. p.s. overall I spent 550gold for all quest line for epic mount, a lot of time, and 8 levels after 60 I was on the slow mount. So think twice.

Just a note, if you wipe on this thing, and no one can rez...the diviner thingy is USED! you have to abandon, go to Stormwind, and get a new one. The instance also has to be reset, because the door to the room closes. I was kinda mad, re-cleared and I was like "Where's the item?..." My 70 friend wasn't too happy....

c.b: You summon the spirits in the same room as Rattlegore stand in. Clear it and place the divination scryer in the NW corner but still on the mound (which rattlegore stand on). Tell your party to stand in the SE corner before you start. As soon as you place the scryer ghosts spawn but they are easy to kill so just run to the other players and kill the ghosts. You can judge seal of wisdom (I used the highest rank on all seals and it worked just fine) to stun them for a few seconds. Also works on the aspect. Second wave isn't too hard either, few elites but can be pulled one and one. Judge seal of justice to stun spirits and the aspect. Third wave is three groups of three elites. Do NOT pull the middle group first. Start with the group by the door and take the middle group last. When you pull the middle group all remaining groups will aggro. Remember to judge seal of righteousness on both spirits and aspect. Might be useful to put the shadow res aura on for the last wave. The last wave was easy too, few elites spawn every now and then. We had to wait a while betweent the spawns. Good time to rest and drink/eat. Use seal of light on spirits and the aspect. When the aspect is killed the boss will spawn. He's easy to kill. Loot the boss, use the charger's lost soul to get the charger's redeemed soul and hand in the quest :) Did it with a 70 hunter, 70 mage, 70 shadow priest, 69 rogue and me, 61 pally. Its really easy when you figure it out and do it right, hope some of you won't have to do the same mistakes we did. If you wipe, abandon the quest, go back to your trainer and take it again. Reset the instance and do it all over again. We couldn't find any other way to finish it. Good luck!

In my experience, the ranks of the judgements do not matter, so go ahead and use you're highest one. just make sure you have them in the right order and your set. I found that setting up a separate casting bar with the seals in the 1-4 order with judgement in the #5 slot helped a great deal.

Solo'd as a 67 retri pala ... the satisfaction was immensely. Getting there First of all, in order to access the basement easy without clearing too much trash you can jump down on the right of the platform, into the corner of the room bellow, as you enter the instance (right before the very first guards). BoP yourself if you want, it's only about 1k health loss. You will be agroed immediately by a group of 3-4 mobs, easy to solo. After this, stay close to wall (walk the edge) and exit through the door on the left; in the next room you don't have to fight anyone (aggro range was small enough at 67), just watch the patrols and you can enter the whelps room safely (door on the left again). In the whelp room hug the left wall and you have to clear through 2 groups of mobs maximum. Basement of the Great Ossuary Range pull with Exorcism the first 2 mobs on left and right and deal with them at the door. You can range pull Rattlegore just the same, but be careful of the mobs wandering behind him so you don't get any add. I wanted to play safe so I used SoL & JoL throughout the fight, spamming CS, DS and consecration. Only had to use 1 mana pot, the instant healing FoL from Art of War was enough to keep me alive (around 24% crit in mixed greens and blues from q rewards). The waves Clear the room of the remaining adds and use the quest item on the mound where Rattlegore was standing. During waves I positioned myself on the corner to the right of the entrance; I was able to drink between waves with no problems, except for the last wave when the dark knight spawns immediately. First wave I used JoW with SoL, second wave JoJ with SoL. Be careful if you chase the mobs from the 2nd wave as they spawn through the room. I wasn't patient and I made the mistake to kill the Aspect from the 2nd wave close to the mound; the result was that the third waves spawned, I aggroed the group from the middle and all the adds came to take a piece of me. I died, had to abandon quest and retake it so I get a new quest item and take it from the beginning of the event. On the 3rd wave use Seal of Rightneouss and judge anything you want, I preferred light. First pull the group from the door, pull the middle group last. For the last wave, the 4th, use shadow res aura, it helps with the shadowbolts. Judge light to stun them and burn them fast (CS, DS, Exorcism), they shouldn't hit you more than once. Be careful where you kill the Aspect from the last wave as the Dark Knight will spawn on top of the mound immediately (you may have time for one quick heal to top you). On the Dark Knight I used SoR and JoL; healing through instant FoL was enough, although one time I BoPed myself to get to top HP to be on the safe side. Finally, claim your charger ... you walked the hard way instead of just training the skill, but you get a nice feeling of accomplishment !

c.b: When it comes to your reward choices there are a couple of things to consider. In my opinion, the Hunting Spear is probably the least useful of the three items. Weapons themselves will eventually become outdated, to begin with, as people level up, especially with the upcoming expansion. Also, if one truly wants a decent spear, many hunters go and get the Ice Barbed Spear (http://www.wowhead.com/?item=19106) which is a reward if you win ONE battle in Alterac Valley. This spear has better overall stats, in my opinion, than the Hunting Spear, as it has an abundance of agility as well as stamina. This brings it down to the last two items. Now if you are a Marks or Surv hunter, the Devilsaur Eye is clearly the best choice for you. However, I'm not certain if there are other trinkets more useful than this for Marks/Surv hunters, so please make a comment if you believe there is. Being a BM hunter, I instinctively went for the Devilsaur Tooth. I have no doubt in my mind that this trinket is one of the best for hunters with this spec. It's highly useful for opening attacks, especially if one has a cat. A cat put into Prowl, with the Devilsaur Tooth buff, as well as triggering Bestial Wrath the moment before it reaches the intended target means a strong critical opening attack that will proc Frenzy instantly. This will become especially useful when the expansion pack is released. One of the new BM abilities is Ferocious Inspiration. It means that when your pet scores a critical hit, all party members have their damage output increased by 1-3% for 10 seconds.

c.b: ...expanding on what glassthorne posted: When this quest was first available, all the way to the release of AQ40, there were no replacements for the Devilsaur Eye, and any hunter who took the spear found it quickly replaced, and any hunter who took the Devilsaur Tooth quickly found that it was useless in raids, and nominal in PvP. However, with the release of AQ40, Naxx, and the expansion, there are several replacements for the Devilsaur Eye. Examples being: Badge of the Swarmguard, Drake Fang Talisman, Jom Gabber, Kiss of the Spider and Slayer's Crest. Even outside of raids, the Earthstrike trinket from the Cenarian Circle replaces the Devilsaur Eye. However, nothing in the game replaces the Devilsaur Tooth. So, if you are a hunter that has not yet chosen your reward, it is probably in your best interest to get the Devilsaur Tooth. Even in the expansion, there is not a replacement for this item.

I think there's too many arguments that exist on the premise of an item being "irreplaceable". It's said also for the warlock quest, with one trinket being pretty much unique and the other two items being eventually replaceable. But that trinket is a 30 minute cooldown free void walker. My problem with taking the "irreplaceable" trinket is that odds are you're not going to wear the thing at higher levels even if you can't replace it. What it does simply isn't special enough to matter. In this case we have the Eye versus the Tooth. The polearm is pretty bad, nice crit, but while leveling your crit isn't terribly high to begin with. Greens at least increase your AP while they're at it. The Tooth gives a free crit on your pet's next attack. Now, if you're MM, or Survival, this doesn't really matter, your pet isn't a huge amount of your DPS and a crit other then the minor extra damage (especially if it's a claw or bite rather then a melee swing) is tiny. But if you're BM, you're looking at Ferocious Inspiration and Frenzy both procing every crit. The problem exists that your pet simply can maintain both up a ridiculously large amount of the time without the trinket. Particularly after the first crit, frenzy helps increase the odds he'll proc before the effect is over and refresh the duration. With cobra reflexes, serpent's swiftness, and frenzy, your pet attacks slightly more then once a second (.99 per second). Combined with a focus dump like Claw, and he doesn't need the crit from the Tooth. I think the Eye is more beneficial while leveling. And odds are if you're looking this up you are doing that. The eye gives a solid benefit and while it's not unique, the fact of the matter is you probably won't be using the Tooth in Outland anyway. You'll end up replacing either trinket but the Eye is a better damage increaser then offering a free crit to a pet that crits all the time anyway.

c.b: I would be inclined to say that of the three the Fire Ruby is hands down the best of the rewards. I think we can agree the mana return on the Glacial Spike is not worthwhile considering other options. The Necklace is easily replaceable as you can see above. The Ruby however, improves your mana efficiency, returning as someone said an average of 250 mana every 3 minutes. This is roughly 7 mp/5, though it will end up being slighly more useful than that as it will come in larger chunks, which could mean an extra cast. The 100 fire spell bonus may seem only useful for Fire mages, but I know that leveling my Frost Mage, there is one fire spell I cast very frequently. Fire Blast! Frost is short on instants, and Cone of Cold is short range and rather mana intensive for a single target. I tend to finish off mobs with Fire Blast even as a full frost mage, as well as make use of the instant cast to do big Frostbolt/ Fire Blast Shatter combos. To make use of this trinket a simple Fire Blast macro can be used to minimize the hassle. /use Fire Ruby /cast Fire Blast As instants get 42.86% spell damage, you'd recieve about an extra 43 damage on Fire Blast whenever the trinket is up, as well as the mana back. An extra 65 damage on a crit in a Frostbolt/Fire Blast shatter combo. Hardly useless for a leveling Frost Mage! I would encourage any leveling Frost Mage to take the Fire Ruby for juicy Shatter combos

c.b: Before the event is triggered, the group will want to go to the corner you'll face by entering the basement and turning right 90 degrees. There are four waves. After each wave, you fight a named mob called "Aspect of ". Wave 1: As soon as the Divination Scryer is placed, 9 or so very slow moving mobs spawn. It is recommended that the shaman kite the slow movers around the room, making them even slower with earthbind totems. The shaman should be able to avoid taking damage the entire time. One of the other party memebers should start pulling each mob off of the shaman one by one and training it to the rest of the group, who should kill it. Kill all 9, a named comes. Make sure that everyone is in the corner mentioned earlier when the named dies. Wave 2: Mobs will spawn one at a time. Once you kill one, another will spawn. Kill all 9-ish, another named appears. Again, make sure you're in the corner when he dies. Wave 3: 3 linked groups of three spawn. It is recommended that you take the group out by the enterence first. If you have a warrior, have him hug the wall and charge one of the three in that group when they are furthest away grom the middle group. If he accidently pulls the middle group, let him die, res, and try again. If he succeeds, the rest of the part should hug the wall to the other side and take out the group of three. Afterwards, take out the middle group, then the far group. Kill all three groups, a third named spawns. Again, make sure you're in the corner when he dies. Wave 4: One mob spawns, then subsequent ones spawn on a timer. It is important to DPS each one as fast as possible, as these hit hard. You can make life easier by dropping a grounding totem, as that will absorb their hard-hitting range spell. If you have two shamans in the party, it makes it MUCH easier. Kill all 9-ish, another named appears. Kill him, Death Knight Darkreaver spawns. Kill him for the win!

Did this at level 20. You will NEED Master of Deception rank 3 for the second key and you need to do this solo. You can pick up the quest at the Dead Drop around 47,71 in Silverpine Forest, just outside Pyrewood Village in a house near Shadowfang Keep. This is where the letter from 'C' sends you, and it is also the same cache you will return to later to complete the quest and for the final payment. In short, you need to get into the courtyard in Shadowfang Keep, pickpocket two specific enemies for two half-keys, combine them into the Twin Key, then use that key to open a chest in the stables for the Horn of Xelthos. To get past the the courtyard door you have two options: You can go to Stonetalon Mountains, pickpocket the Venture Co. Work Order from Venture Co. enemies in the Windshear Crag and bring it to Veenix, who gives you the Breaching Charge. You can then use that to blow open the courtyard door in Shadowfang Keep. Or you can open the prison cell and talk to the NPC. If you do it that way, you’re going to die, but once he opens the door it stays open when you run back. Once you’re through, you need to pickpocket two enemies that only spawn when doing this solo: Gemela is in the dining hall where Baron Silverlaine is, just inside from the kitchen. Pickpocket her for the Sister’s Half-Key. Gefell is further on, go up the stairs past Silverlaine and take the right instead of the normal route left. He is in the first room around the corner. Pickpocket him for the Brother’s Half-Key. Once you have both halves, find somewhere safe and combine them into the Twin Key. Keep in mind that combining them will take you out of stealth. Then go back down to the courtyard and into the stables. There is an Ornamented Chest in there, open it with the Twin Key and you’ll get the Horn of Xelthos. Also, the reward doesn’t show up straight away. After you finish the quest at the cache, go to a major city. You’ll get another mail from 'C' saying your payment is waiting in the cache again. Go back there and you can pick up the Pyrewood Signet Ring.

Step 1 After reaching Level 30, you'll get mail that you can get a new Quest at Pyrewood Village (47.1 , 71.1) - Same location as the Horn of Xelthos Quest Step 2 Go behind the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades into the Stables (81.2 , 32.1) - you will find a Chest there providing you with Scarlet's Initiate Uniform Step 3 Go into the Graveyard and find a Scarlet Scryer , Pickpocket that NPC for Scryers Key Note: You can already use your Scarlets Initiate Uniform here, but once you enter Stealth you will drop the disguise anyways Step 4 Leave the Graveyard section and head into the Libary (across the Hall of the Scarlet Monastery), Put on your Scarlets Initiate Uniform, Head into the Second to Last Room and Loot the Personal Letterbox for Confidential Message Step 5 Go back to the Graveyard - go to the actual graveyard Section and on the left and right side you will find a bench on each side of the dungeon - /sit on that (you can do that in stealth Once you /sit on either bench you should see a message in the chatbox You hear a faint click twice (once per bench) and then You hear the sound of stone moving - that way you know it worked. Then just ahead in the mausoleum you see a Chest that you can loot for the Reliquary Key. If a Elite Ghost is guarding the Chest, go outside the Graveyard and reset the instance. There is a chance of no Monster in front of the Chest or just a non-elite Ghost. Note: If you reset the instance you have to sit on the benches again to activate the mechanism Step 6 Go to the Library once more, put on your disguise, head to the first small room on the left in the latter part of the dungeon, loot the chest for Eye of Bhossca Step 7 Go Back to(47.1 , 71.1) and turn in the quest Go to any Major City and you will receive Mail from 'C' that you can pick up your reward, once again in Pyrewood Village (47.1 , 71.1) Go back to the Chest / Dead Drop in Pyrewood Village (47.1 , 71.1) to pick up your reward Ruby-Adorned Blade Enjoy!

c.b: Step-by-Step Solo Route Get your disguise: Before entering either wing, grab the Scarlet Initiate's Uniform disguise from the Supply Locker chest in the stables outside the monastery. Wing 1 - Graveyard (Left Portal): Put on your disguise and head into the Graveyard. Go to the first large room (Chamber of Atonement) and Pick Pocket a Scarlet Scryer (or Scarlet Crier) to get the Scryer's Key. Wing 2 - Library (Right Portal): Leave the Graveyard and enter the Library wing. Proceed to the Athenaeum section to find the Personal Letterbox. Open it with your Scryer's Key to find a Confidential Message instructing you to "sit on the benches between the two statues" back in the Graveyard. Back to the Graveyard: Return to the Graveyard wing. Follow the instructions from the note to sit on the benches, then head into the northern mausoleum (Forlorn Cloister) to loot a Stone Coffer for the Reliquary Key. Back to the Library: Return to the Library wing one last time. Go deep into the dungeon to the Gallery of Treasures and use your new key to open the Padlocked Reliquary to loot the Eye of Bhossca.
